topic.name: Irrecoverable Debts & Provision for Doubtful Debts

parts.problem_md:
Mary sells goods on credit and maintains a provision for doubtful debts. She wants to decrease her provision for doubtful debts by \$650. Which journal entry records this decrease in the provision for doubtful debts? | | | debit

\$ | credit

\$ | |---|---|---|---| | **A** | credit customer

income statement | 650 | 650 | | **B** | income statement

credit customer | 650 | 650 | | **C** | income statement

provision for doubtful debts | 650 | 650 | | **D** | provision for doubtful debts

income statement | 650 | 650 |
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D**

- When a provision for doubtful debts is set up, or when its balance is increased, then

  - The amount is debited to the income statement as an expense
  - And a corresponding credit entry is made in the provision for doubtful debts account
- Here however the provision for doubtful debts balance is being decreased, so Mary should do the opposite

  - Debit the amount to the provision for doubtful debts account
  - And credit the income statement

**A** and **B** are incorrect; provision for doubtful debts does not involve entries in credit customer accounts (writing off a debt as irrecoverable, on the other hand, does affect the relevant credit customer account)

**C** is incorrect; debit and credit are the wrong way round

parts.problem_md:
Gerdan Duo Limited maintains a provision for doubtful debts account. This account had a balance of \$5 400 on 1 January 2023.

The provision should have been decreased to \$4 100 on 31 December 2023, but this adjustment was not made.

What was the effect of this error on the retained earnings in the statement of financial position on 31 December 2023?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- On 31 December 2023 the provision for doubtful debts should have been lowered to \$4100

  - Instead it was kept at \$5400
  - That means that the provision on 31 December 2023 was too high by
  
    - \$5400 - \$4100 = \$1300
- Consider the effect of that on the profit for the year

  - Decreasing the provision increases the profit
  - Therefore, overstating the provision for doubtful debts will understate the profit for the year
- Now consider the effect on retained earnings

  - Retained earnings = opening balance + profit for the year - dividends paid - transfer to general reserve
  - So understating the profit for the year will also understate the retained earnings
  
    - Because you are adding less to the opening balance

**A** is incorrect; the amount is correct, but the retained earnings were understated not overstated

**B** and **D** are incorrect; \$4100 is the correct provision amount for 31 December 2023, but it is not the amount by which the retained earnings were affected by the error

parts.problem_md:
Janet maintains a provision for doubtful debts of 6% of trade payables, calculated at the end of each financial year.

On 1 April 2023 the balance on her provision for doubtful debts account was \$648.

On 31 March 2024 trade receivables owed \$4 000 less than they owed on 31 March 2023.

How did the change in the provision for doubtful debts affect the profit for the year ended 31 March 2024?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- You can figure the change in the provision for doubtful debts directly

  - Trade receivables owed \$4000 less on 31 March 2024 than they did on 31 March 2023
  - That means the provision for doubtful debts should decrease by 6% of \$4000
  
    - \$4000 ✕ 6% = \$240 decrease
- You could also figure that out 'the long way'

  - \$648 is 6% of the trade receivables balance for 1 April 2023
  - So the trade receivables balance on that date was
  
    - \$648 ÷ 6% = \$10 800
  - On 31 March 2024 it was \$4000 less than that
  
    - \$10 800 - \$4000 = \$6800
  - And 6% of that balance is
  
    - \$6800 ✕ 6% = \$408
  - Which is a decrease of
  
    - \$648 - \$408 = \$240
- Next figure out how a \$240 decrease in provision for doubtful debts would affect the profit for the year

  - Decreasing the provision increases the profit because fewer funds are being set aside to cover doubtful debts
  - So decreasing the provision for doubtful debts will increase the profit for the year

**A** is incorrect; this is the correct amount, but it is identified as a decrease instead of an increase

**C** and **D** are incorrect; \$408 is the new balance on the provision for doubtful debts account, but this is not the amount by which the profit for the year changes

parts.problem_md:
On 4 April, Onni wrote off \$375 owed to him by Marial, a credit customer, as being irrecoverable.

On 2 November, Marial paid \$150 by cheque in part settlement of that debt.

Which entries should Onni make on 2 November?

|   | account to be debited | amount to be credited |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | bank | debts recovered |
| **B** | bank | irrecoverable debts |
| **C** | debts recovered | bank |
| **D** | irrecoverable debts | bank |
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- The payment from Marial will increase the balance in the bank account

  - Bank is an asset account
  
    - So a transaction that increases it should be entered as a debit
  - This rules out answers C and D
- The corresponding credit entry will be made in the debts recovered account

  - Be careful here; individual debts recovered are *not* recorded in the irrecoverable debts account

**B** is incorrect; recovery of debts written off is not recorded in the irrecoverable debts account

**C** is incorrect; debit and credit are the wrong way round

**D** is incorrect; bank should be debited not credited, and recovery of debts written off is not recorded in the irrecoverable debts account

parts.problem_md:
Danny's books included the following balances on 1 November 2023.

|   | \$ |
|---|---|
| trade receivables | 85 600 |
| provision for doubtful debt | 2 568 |

Trade receivables at 31 October 2024 were \$79 200,* *of which \$600 should be written off as irrecoverable.

Danny wants to maintain his provision for doubtful debts at 3% of trade receivables.

What was the change in the provision for doubtful debts at 31 October 2024?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- First find what the provision for doubtful debts balance should be on 31 October 2024

  - Subtract \$600 from the trade receivables amount for the irrecoverable debt
  
    - This debt is to be written off
    - Therefore no provision for doubtful debts needs to be made for it
  - So the amount provision for doubtful debts needs to be made for is
  
    - \$79 200 - \$600 = \$78 600
  - Find 3% of that amount
  
    - \$78 600 ✕ 3% = \$2358
- So the provision for doubtful debts balance should be \$2358 on 31 October 2024

  - But on 1 November 2023 it was \$2568
  - That is greater than the amount needed on 31 October 2024
  - So that amount needs to be decreased by \$2568 - \$2358 = \$210

**A** is incorrect; this is the amount you would get if you didn't subtract the \$600 for irrecoverable debts first

**C** is incorrect; this is what you get if you subtract the correct answer from \$600

**D** is incorrect; this is what you get if you subtract \$192 (answer A) from \$600

parts.problem_md:
A business maintains a provision for doubtful debts of 4% of trade receivables. The balance on the provision for doubtful debts account on 31 December 2022 was \$2 500.

On 31 December 2023 the trade receivables amounted to \$70 000.

How will the required adjustment to the provision for doubtful debts be recorded?

|   | provision for doubtful debts account | \$ | income statement | \$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | credit | 300 | added to gross profit | 300 |
| **B** | credit | 300 | deducted from gross profit | 300 |
| **C** | debit | 300 | added to gross profit | 300 |
| **D** | debit | 300 | deducted from gross profit | 300 |
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B** - First determine whether the balance on the provision for doubtful debts account needs to be increased or decreased on 31 December 2023 - Find 4% of the trade receivables amount on that date - \$70 000 ✕ 4% = \$2800 - The provision for doubtful debts balance should be \$2800 on 31 December 2023 - But on 31 December 2022 it was only \$2500 - So it needs to be increased by \$2800 - \$2500 = \$300 - The provision for doubtful debts balance is increasing - This increase is an expense for the business - It is debited to the income statement as an expense - This means it will be deducted from the gross profit - It is credited to the provision for doubtful debts account - Here is the provision for doubtful debts account | Date | Detail | \$ | Date | Detail | \$ | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 2023
Dec 31 | Balancec/d | 2 800 | 2023
Jan 1 | Balance b/d | 2 500 | | | | | Dec 31 | Income statement | 300 | | | | 2 800 | | | 2 800 | **A** is incorrect; the \$300 is deducted from the gross profit, not added **C** is incorrect; the \$300 is credited to the provision for doubtful debts account (not debited), and deducted from the gross profit (not added) **D** is incorrect; the \$300 is credited to the provision for doubtful debts account, not debited

parts.problem_md:
Louhi made the following entries in her ledger.

| account debited | account credited |
|---|---|
| irrecoverable debts | Jaden |

What was she recording?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- An irrecoverable debt occurs when a business is unable to receive payment from a credit customer for the amount they owe

  - The relevant trade receivables account is credited in the sales ledger
  
    - The amount they owe is decreasing
    - So that asset is worth less to the company
  - The irrecoverable debts account is debited in the nominal ledger

**A** is incorrect; failing to pay by a particular date does not necessarily mean that a debt is irrecoverable

**B** is incorrect; a recovered debt that had been written off would never be recorded by a credit entry in the trade payable account

**D** is incorrect; irrecoverable debt has to do with a business and its customers, not a business and its suppliers

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: A credit customer has failed to pay by an agreed-upon date

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: A debt has been recovered which had previously been written off

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: An amount owed by a credit customer cannot be recovered

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: Louhi has been unable to pay her supplier

parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Maximum 2 marks for reasons such as:
> 
> - It is likely that some trade receivables will not pay the amount they owe
> - To apply the accounting principle of prudence by ensuring profit is not overstated
> - To apply the accounting principle of prudence by ensuring trade receivables is not overstated
> - To apply the accounting principle of matching by ensuring that sales which are unlikely to be received are taken into account for the year that the sales took place

parts.problem_md:
Logan is a trader who sells goods on credit. His year end is 30 September. Logan has provided the following information.

|   | \$ |
|---|---|
| At 1 October 2022 |   |
| Trade receivables | 7 500 |
| 1 June 2023 | 2 490 |
| At 30 September 2023 |   |
| Trade receivables | 8 700 |
| Irrecoverable debts to be written off | 325 |

The provision for doubtful debts is to be maintained at 4% of trade receivables.

**REQUIRED**

Prepare the provision for doubtful debts account for the year ended 30 September 2023. Balance the account at 30 September 2023 and bring down the balance at 1 October 2023.

Logan 
Provision for doubtful debts account

| Date | Details | \$ | Date | Details | \$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
parts.solution_md:
Calculate the provision at the start of the year

$4 \% \times 7500 = 300$

Calculate the provision at the end of the year

- Subtract the irrecoverable debts

$8700-325=8375$

- Find the provision

$4 \% \times 8375 = 335$

Calculate the increase

$335-300=35$

Logan 
Provision for doubtful debts account

| Date | Details | \$ | Date | Details | \$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 |   |   | 2022 |   |   |
| Sep 30 | Balance c/d **[1]** | 335 | Oct 1 | Balance b/d **[1]** | 300 |
|   |   |   | 2023 |   |   |
|   |   |   | Sep 30 | Income statement **[1]** | 35 |
|   |   | <u>335</u> |   |   | <u>335</u> |
|   |   |   | Oct 1 | Balance b/d **[1]** | 335 |

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 4 marks in total:
> 
> - 1 mark for the correct balance b/d
> - 1 mark for the correct balance c/d
> - 1 mark for using your **own figure** to find the amount for the income statement
> - 1 mark for using your **own figure** for balance c/d to create the balance b/d

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't forget to subtract the irrecoverable debts before calculating the provision for doubtful debts.

parts.problem_md:
Stalla is a sole trader who sells on credit. She maintains a provision for doubtful debts at 4% of trade receivables.

Stalla’s trade receivables were:

|   | \$ |
|---|---|
| At 31 December 2021 | 75 000 |
| At 31 December 2022 | 77 000 |

**REQUIRED **

Prepare Stalla’s provision for doubtful debts account for the year ended 31 December 2022. Balance the account at 31 December 2022 and bring down the balance at 1 January 2023.

Stalla 
Provision for doubtful debts account

| Date | Details | \$ | Date | Details | \$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
|   |   |   |   |   |   |
parts.solution_md:
Find the provision for doubtful debts at the start of the year

$4 \% \times 75000 = 3000$

Find the provision for doubtful debts at the end of the year

$4 \% \times 77000 = 3080$

Find the increase in the provision for doubtful debts

$3080-3000=80$

Stalla 
Provision for doubtful debts account

| Date | Details | \$ | Date | Details | \$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 |   |   | 2022 |   |   |
| Dec 31 | Balance c/d | 3 080 | Jan 1 | Balance b/d **[1]** | 3 000 |
|   |   |   | Dec 31 | Income statement **[1]** | 80 |
|   |   | <u>3 080</u> |   |   | <u>3 080</u> |
|   |   |   | 2023 |   |   |
|   |   |   | Jan 1 | Balance b/d **[1]** | 3 080 |

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 3 marks in total. 1 mark for the correct date, details and amount(s) for each of the items below.
> 
> **Explanation**
> 
> - 1 Jan 2022: \$3000 as the balance b/d on the credit side
> 
>   - It is a credit because it is a provision for the reduction in an asset balance
> - 31 Dec 2022: Make an entry on the credit side for the income statement
> 
>   - This mark is for subtracting your **own figures **for the starting and ending balances
> - 1 Jan 2023: \$3080 as the balance b/d on the credit side
